summary: Illustrative narrative for a FEATURE job. The executable stage order is loaded from team/pipelines/feature.pipeline.json by src/agents/pipeline.ts. This file is not imported by the runner and must not be treated as an executable workflow definition. Defects and incidents follow their own registered pipelines.

example_job.text: Build a wallet management dashboard for Thirdeye, with EVM and Solana support.

steps.title: Intake and decomposition
steps.does: Identify the domain, classify the job (feature, bugfix or incident), set the priority, and create one subtask per owning unit.
steps.gate: Every subtask names exactly one owner and one dependency; the job names the pipeline it follows.
steps.example: Domain is wallet management, class is feature, priority set; subtasks created for product, architect, blockchain, backend, frontend, qa, sentinel, devops.

steps.title: Define what success means
steps.does: Write the acceptance criteria as observations a tester can check, and state what is out of scope.
steps.gate: Each criterion is an observable outcome and at least one out-of-scope line exists.
steps.example: Supported wallet types, connection flows, balances, transaction history and account-linking requirements.

steps.title: Design the implementation
steps.does: Decide the adapters, API contract, data model, ownership verification and security boundaries before code exists.
steps.gate: An API contract the frontend can build against, a data model, and the failure modes the design accepts.
steps.example: Wallet adapters for EVM and Solana, APIs, data models, ownership verification and security boundaries.

steps.title: Build in parallel where dependencies permit
steps.does: Wallet domain rules, the service and the dashboard are built against the agreed API contract at the same time, each behind a pull request.
steps.gate: Each pull request touches only its unit's owned paths and none touches main.
steps.example: Blockchain specialist handles the wallet domain rules, backend builds the service, frontend builds the dashboard.
steps.money_boundary: tdt_blockchain may specify and review money paths but any transaction or signer change needs the owner.

steps.title: Test the entire feature
steps.does: Verify against the acceptance criteria, not only the diff, marking each met or unmet with its evidence.
steps.gate: Wallet linking, authentication, chain switching, wrong-network handling, unauthorized access and UI behaviour each have a result and the suite count is attached.
steps.example: Linking, authentication, chain switching, incorrect network handling, unauthorized access and UI behaviour.

steps.title: Challenge the implementation
steps.does: Attack the design and the diff: ownership proofs, signatures, secret handling, transaction authorization and data isolation.
steps.gate: Named findings with severity and an exploit path, or an explicit statement that there are none, plus a negative test that proves each refusal.
steps.example: Wallet ownership, signatures, secret handling, transaction authorization and data isolation.

steps.title: Release readiness
steps.does: Verify integration, CI, a preview deployment, rollback readiness and release authorization.
steps.gate: CI green on the exact head, a preview that serves the change, a rollback step written down, and the owner's approval recorded before production.
steps.example: Verify integration, CI, preview deployment, rollback readiness and release authorization.

steps.title: Release to production
steps.does: Promote the verified change and prove it is live: merge, deployment id, sha matching HEAD, health check green.
steps.gate: Deployment id and sha matching HEAD, plus a health check on the deployed path. Needs the owner's approval.
steps.example: Merge to main, Vercel production deployment READY, sha matching HEAD, healthz 200.

steps.title: Accept and close
steps.does: Confirm every acceptance criterion has evidence, confirm the production release actually happened, update the task, and schedule any follow-up work that remains.
steps.gate: Every acceptance criterion points at the evidence that decided it, including the deployment id and sha that prove the production release; unmet criteria become named follow-up tasks.
steps.example: All acceptance criteria have evidence, the task is updated and remaining follow-up work is scheduled.

rules.single_owner: Each step has one accountable owner; contributors help but do not share accountability.
rules.no_self_acceptance: The unit that builds never performs steps 5, 6 or 8 on its own work.
rules.failure_returns: A failed gate returns the job to the producing step with the failure attached; it is never skipped or silently passed.
rules.escalation: Money, merge, deploy, deletion, public claims and membership changes stop at the owner.
rules.evidence_over_report: HERMES closes on artifacts and run evidence, not on a unit's statement that it is done.
rules.scope: Feature jobs only. A defect or an incident is routed to its own pipeline by HERMES at intake.
